feature.title: Masks
feature.summary: Override channel and step trig, note, velocity, length and chord values.
feature.prose:
Masks override attributes of the merged pattern data. They can overwrite pattern values or create steps the patterns do not have, and they accept triggers, notes, velocities and chords. Set a channel default to affect every step, or hold a step to set an individual override. Unset attributes use the channel default or merged pattern data. Each Masks recipe below starts from the four-step loop in Make your first loop (channel 1, pattern 1, steps 1-4). A masked value always wins over the pattern for that step; the channel default wins over the pattern for every step without its own mask.
The Masks screen shows the value you are editing as you turn E3, with note names for the Note row, so stop on the readout instead of counting detents. One detent moves a note by one MIDI note and other values by one unit.

[Masks demo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J1ckUZvhFJ0&t=1740s)
feature.musical_use: Set a note mask to change the pitch of one step while the pattern keeps its rhythm; set a velocity mask to accent or soften a step; fill the Chd rows to add chord voices; add a trig mask to put a note on an empty step. To run channels at different lengths, see Channel Length.

details.title: Unset values and precedence
details.text: X is an unset attribute, not zero. A step's explicit attribute wins over the channel default; an unset step uses the default; an unset default falls back to merged pattern data. Clearing step overrides does not erase the defaults.

details.title: Chord masks
details.text: Chd1–Chd4 add four scale-relative voices above or below the root. 3rd and 5th specify intervals, not MIDI note numbers. From X, turn E3 right for a voice above the root and left for a voice below it; each row reaches 14 scale steps either way. Select a polyphonic output to play simultaneous chord voices. Use strum and chord velocity to adjust their timing and level.

details.title: Scale, degree and rotation
details.text: Note masks snap to the selected scale by default. Degree and rotation apply only when full quantisation is enabled. See Snap Note Masks to Scale, Quantise Note Masks and Fully Quantise Mask for their precedence. Turn off Snap note masks to scale in the Mosaic params to enter accidentals or dissonant notes.

details.title: MIDI and clearing
details.text: Hold a step and play a MIDI keyboard to enter notes and chords. Live recording also enters masks. With a step held, K2 clears that step even if K1 is held. Other channels are unaffected.

details.title: If a new note is silent
details.text: Check the selected channel's output, active range and mute state. A trig alone needs an audible note, velocity and length. A mono voice cannot sound all chord voices together. To undo an exception, hold that step and press K2.

details.title: Note names on the Masks screen
details.text: The Masks screen uses norns musicutil: floor(MIDI note / 12 − 2). MIDI note 60 is displayed as C3. The Fixed Note parameter uses a different label convention and displays MIDI note 60 as C5. Use numeric MIDI notes when comparing these controls.

recipes.title: Try a different ending for a four-note melody
recipes.text:
Starting point: the four-step loop from Make your first loop. Channel 1 plays pattern 1 on steps 1-4 with channel defaults Note C3 (MIDI 60), Vel 80 and Len 1/2, so it repeats one note four times. The Masks screen shows the note name for the value you are editing, and one detent of E3 moves one MIDI note, so turn E3 until the screen reads the name given below instead of counting. Norns shows MIDI 60 as C3, so 72 is C4, 74 is D4, 76 is E4 and 79 is G4.

1. Open Channel tasks with E1, turn E2 to Masks and press K3. Turn E2 to Note. The header reads NOTE MASKS CH01 and, with no step held, the Note row shows the channel default, C3.

2. Hold step 1 (grid (1,4)). The header gains ST01, which means edits now apply to that step only. Turn E3 right until the screen reads C4 (12 detents), then release the step.

3. Hold step 2 (2,4), turn E3 right until the screen reads D4 (14 detents) and release the step.

4. Hold step 3 (3,4), turn E3 right until the screen reads G4 (19 detents) and release the step.

5. Hold step 4 (4,4), turn E3 right until the screen reads E4 (16 detents) and release the step. After each release the screen goes back to the channel default, C3; each step you set keeps its own note.

6. Tap Play at (1,8). The loop plays C4, D4, G4, E4 (72, 74, 79, 76). Tap Play again to stop.

7. Hold step 4 and turn E3 left until the screen reads D4 (two detents). Release the step and tap Play: the phrase now ends C4, D4, G4, D4. Only step 4 changed; steps 1-3 keep their masks. Tap Play to stop.

8. To end on the root instead, hold step 4 and turn E3 left until the screen reads C4 (two more detents). Release the step and tap Play: the phrase is C4, D4, G4, C4.

All of these notes are in the default C major scale, so scale snapping leaves them unchanged. A note outside the scale is moved onto it. The captured example "Change the ending of a four-note melody" runs steps 1 to 8 on the four-note loop and shows the MIDI strip after each change (its pattern keeps its own velocities, so the recipe's Vel 80 is not repeated there); "Set channel and step note masks" shows the same hold-and-turn gestures on a different loop.

recipes.title: Add a ghost note before an accent
recipes.text:
Starting point: the four-step loop from Make your first loop, with channel default Vel 80. A ghost note is a very quiet note played just before a louder one; it makes the louder note feel pushed.

1. Open Channel tasks with E1, turn E2 to Masks and press K3. Turn E2 to Vel. With no step held the screen reads 80, the channel default.

2. Hold step 3 (grid (3,4)) and turn E3 right until the screen reads 100. Release the step. Step 3 is now the accent.

3. Hold step 2 (2,4) and turn E3 left until the screen reads 35. Release the step. Step 2 is the ghost note.

4. Tap Play at (1,8). The velocities are 80, 35, 100, 80: a soft tap on step 2 leads into the loud step 3. Tap Play again to stop.

The captured example "Set a ghost note and an accent" shows steps 1 to 4 and the velocities 80, 35, 100, 80 in the MIDI strip (that loop plays C, D, E and F, not one repeated note); "Set velocity and length masks" shows the Vel row and the MIDI velocities each edit produces. To make the ghost note come and go, continue with Make the ghost note intermittent.

recipes.title: Make the ghost note intermittent
recipes.text:
Starting point: the ghost-note loop from Add a ghost note before an accent (step 2 at velocity 35, step 3 at 100). Velocity decides how loud a note is; Trig Probability decides whether the trig plays at all.

1. Open Channel tasks with E1, turn E2 to Trig params and press K3. The screen shows all ten slots at once. A slot that has no parameter assigned yet is an empty slot.

2. Turn E2 to the first empty slot. E2 stops at slot 1 and at slot 10.

3. Press K2, turn E3 until Trig Probability appears, press K3 to assign it and press K2 to return to slot selection. The slot now carries Trig Probability.

4. Hold step 2 (grid (2,4)) and turn E3 until the screen reads 50. Release the step. Step 2 now has its own probability of 50; the other steps use the channel default and still play every time.

5. Tap Play at (1,8) and listen over several passes: the ghost note sounds on about half of them and the other three notes never drop out. Tap Play again to stop.

6. To remove the exception, hold step 2 on Trig params and press K2. This clears every parameter lock on that step.

Steps 1 to 3 (moving to an empty slot and assigning Trig Probability) are shown screen by screen in the captured example "Turn chance into explicit rests".

recipes.title: Add chord voices over a bass
recipes.text:
Starting point: the four-step loop from Make your first loop on channel 1, and a second channel for the chord. Channel 1's device can be monophonic. Channel 2 needs a polyphonic device, because one step plays several notes together. The audio example "A bass with room above it" below plays the same idea with Polyperc 1 for the bass and Doubledecker for the chords; its notes and levels differ from the values used here.

Set up the bass on channel 1.

1. Tap (1,1) to select channel 1. Open Channel tasks with E1, turn E2 to Masks and press K3.

2. With no step held, set Note to C2 (MIDI 48), Vel to 70 and Len to 1/2. Channel 1 now plays bass notes on steps 1-4.

Set up the chord channel.

3. Tap (2,1) to select channel 2. Open Channel tasks, choose Device and pick a polyphonic voice; press K3 to apply it.

4. Assign pattern 1 to channel 2: tap pattern slot (1,2).

5. Set channel 2 to the same four steps: hold step 1 (1,4), tap step 4 (4,4), then release step 1.

6. On Masks, with no step held, set channel 2's Note to C3 (MIDI 60), Vel to 60 and Len to 1/2. It now plays single notes over the bass.

Add the chord voices.

7. Turn E2 to Chd1 and, with no step held, turn E3 two detents to 3rd. Every step adds the scale third above its root: 64.

8. Turn E2 to Chd2 and turn E3 four detents to 5th. Every step adds the scale fifth: 67.

9. Tap Play at (1,8). Channel 2 plays C3, E3 and G3 (60, 64, 67) together on every step over the bass C2 (48). Tap Play again to stop.

Change the voicing.

10. Turn E2 to Chd3 and set 6th (five detents): the chord adds A (69). Hold a single step and change a Chd row to give only that step a different voicing.

Chd values are scale intervals above the root, not MIDI note numbers. In another scale the same 3rd and 5th give that scale's intervals. The captured example "Set chord masks" shows each Chd edit and the MIDI notes it produces.

scenes.title: Set channel and step note masks

steps.caption: Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 on steps 1-4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, and no masks are set. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3, then turn E2 to Note. The header reads NOTE MASKS CH01 and the value reads X, which means no mask is set, so each step plays its own pattern note.

With no step held, turn E3 right until the screen reads G3 (MIDI 67). The screen shows the note name, so stop on the readout. This is the channel note mask: all four steps now play G, and their velocities stay as they were.

Hold step 1 at (1,4). The header gains ST01, which means edits now apply to that step only. Turn E3 right until the screen reads C4 (MIDI 72, five detents up from G3). Step 1 has its own note, which overrides the channel default.
Release step 1. The header loses ST01 and the screen returns to the channel default, G3. Playback now starts with C4 (72) and continues G, G, G: a step mask beats the channel mask.
Hold step 2 at (2,4), turn E3 right until the screen reads D4 (MIDI 74) and release the step. Steps 1 and 2 each have their own note (C4, D4), and steps 3 and 4 still play the channel note G.
Hold step 1 and press K2, then release the step. Step 1's mask is cleared, so it plays G3 again from the channel default, and step 2 still plays D4.
With no step held, hold K1 and press K2. Every step exception is cleared at once and the channel default stays: the screen still reads G3 and all four steps play G again.

Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 on steps 1-4 with the notes C, D, E and F at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, and no masks are set. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, scroll to Masks and press K3, then turn E2 to Vel. The value reads X: there is no channel velocity mask, so every step plays the velocity it has in pattern 1. X means inherit.

With no step held, turn E3 right until the screen reads 50. This channel velocity mask replaces the pattern's velocities: every note now plays at 50, so the whole phrase is softer. Pitch and timing are unchanged.

Hold step 1 at (1,4), turn E3 right until the screen reads 90 and release the step. A step mask overrides the channel mask, so step 1 plays at 90 as an accent while steps 2 to 4 keep the channel velocity of 50. The screen goes back to the channel value, 50.

Hold step 2 at (2,4) and keep holding it. Turn E3 left until the screen reads 0. Velocity 0 is a silent step, which is different from X: X means inherit and still plays. Step 2 is now muted, so a pass plays steps 1, 3 and 4 only. Step 2 is still held in this frame.
Release step 2. The screen returns to 50, but step 2 stays silent: read the MIDI strip, where the loop plays C3 (60) at 90, then E3 (64) and F3 (65) at 50, and step 2's D is missing.
Hold step 2 again, press K2 to clear its masks and release it. The step mask is gone, so step 2 plays at the channel velocity of 50 again and step 1 keeps its accent at 90: velocities 90, 50, 50, 50.
With no step held, turn E2 to Len and turn E3 right until the screen reads 1/2. All four notes now have a half-step gate. The velocities stay at 90, 50, 50 and 50.

Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 on steps 1-4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) and no masks are set. Turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3, then turn E2 to Chd1. The four chord rows Chd1-Chd4 add voices above each step's root, and X means no voice.

With no step held, turn E3 right until the screen reads 3rd (two detents). Every step now plays its root and the scale third above it: 60+64, 62+65, 64+67, 65+69. Chord values are scale intervals, not MIDI numbers. Read the MIDI strip: each step sends its root and its chord note together.
Hold step 1 (grid (1,4)) and turn E3 right until the screen reads 5th (two more detents). Step 1 now plays 60 and 67; the screen shows 5th while the step is held.

Release step 1. The screen shows the channel default 3rd again, but step 1 keeps its own fifth: the phrase is 60+67, then 62+65, 64+67, 65+69. Read the MIDI strip: step 1 sends 60 and 67 together, the other steps their roots and thirds.
Hold step 1, press K2 and release the step. The fifth is cleared and step 1 returns to the channel third: 60+64, then 62+65, 64+67, 65+69.

scenes.title: Change the ending of a four-note melody

steps.caption: Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 on steps 1-4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, and no masks are set. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3, then turn E2 to Note. The value reads X.
With no step held, turn E3 right until the screen reads C3 (MIDI 60). The channel note replaces the pattern's notes, so the MIDI strip shows C3 four times; the velocities stay the pattern's.
Hold step 1 at (1,4), turn E3 right until the screen reads C4 (12 detents) and release the step. The screen goes back to C3, and the loop now starts on C4 (72) before three C3 notes.
Hold step 2 at (2,4), turn E3 right until it reads D4 (14 detents) and release. The MIDI strip shows 72, 74, 60, 60.
Hold step 3 at (3,4), turn E3 right until it reads G4 (19 detents) and release. The MIDI strip shows 72, 74, 79, 60.
Hold step 4 at (4,4), turn E3 right until it reads E4 (16 detents) and release. The melody ends on E4: 72, 74, 79, 76.
Hold step 4 and turn E3 left until it reads D4 (two detents), then release. Only step 4 changed: the phrase now ends 72, 74, 79, 74.
Hold step 4 and turn E3 left two more detents until it reads C4, then release. The phrase ends on the root: 72, 74, 79, 72.

scenes.title: Set a ghost note and an accent

steps.caption: Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 on steps 1-4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, and no masks are set. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3, then turn E2 to Vel. The value reads X.

With no step held, turn E3 right until the screen reads 80. The channel velocity replaces the pattern's velocities: every note plays at 80. This loop plays C, D, E and F, not one repeated note, so read the pitches in the MIDI strip.
Hold step 3 at (3,4), turn E3 right until the screen reads 100 and release. Step 3 is the accent: the MIDI strip shows 80, 80, 100, 80.
Hold step 2 at (2,4), turn E3 left until the screen reads 35, and keep holding. The ST02 readout shows this step exception before you release it.
Release step 2. The screen returns to the channel default 80, while the step exception remains. The MIDI phrase is 80, 35, 100, 80: the quiet ghost note leads into the accent.

Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 in an eight-step loop. Steps 1-4 hold four notes and steps 5-8 are empty. No masks are set. Open Channel tasks with E1, turn E2 to Masks and press K3, then turn E2 to Note. The value reads X.

With no step held, turn E3 right until Note reads C3 (MIDI 60). The channel default replaces the pattern's notes on every step, so all four steps now play C3: read the MIDI strip, which shows C3 four times at the velocities the pattern already had (127, 117, 107, 97).
Turn E2 to Vel and turn E3 right until it reads 80. The channel velocity replaces the pattern's velocities too: the MIDI strip now shows C3 at velocity 80 four times.

Turn E2 to Len and turn E3 right until it reads 1/2. The four notes now have a half-step gate. A trig mask has no pattern note of its own, so a trig you add next will use these three channel defaults.
Return to the channel Note field before setting Step 5.
Hold Step 5 and set its stored note to E3.
Release Step 5. Its E3 note is stored, but the step still has no trig, so the loop keeps playing the four C3 notes.

Turn E2 back to Note. Hold step 5 at (5,4), turn E3 right four detents until the screen reads E3 (MIDI 64) and release it. Step 5 now has its own note, but it still has no trig, so nothing new sounds. Then hold K1 and tap step 5, release the step, then release K1. A trig mask now forces step 5 on, so the loop plays a fifth note after the four notes on steps 1-4: E3 (64) at velocity 80, shown in the MIDI strip and by the new lit step 5 on the grid.

Hold K1 and tap step 5 again, release the step, then release K1. The same gesture toggles the trig mask off, so the loop returns to four C3 notes on steps 1-4. Step 5 keeps its note mask but has no trig, so it stays silent.
Starting point: pattern 1 plays C3, D3, E3 and F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65). Open Channel tasks → Masks → Note. With no step held, the Note value is X, so each step uses its merged pattern note.
With no step held, turn E3 right until Note reads G3 (MIDI 67). All four steps now play G3 while retaining the source-pattern velocities.
With no step held, turn E3 left until Note reads X. The channel mask is unset, so MIDI returns to the pattern's C3, D3, E3 and F3 notes at their original velocities.

audio.title: Small hours · four bars in C major
audio.description: Four bars in C major at 90 BPM. Channel 1 uses Polyperc for bass notes. Channel 2 uses Doubledecker with 3rd and 5th chord masks. The channels have separate note positions, velocities and lengths.
